questions.question: Which statement best matches the lesson idea of electromagnetic radiation?
questions.explanation: The lesson focuses on this objective: describe em radiation as energy from vibrating charges.
options: Describe EM radiation as energy from vibrating charges
Only memorize the title without using evidence
Ignore diagrams when explaining Physics
Use household outlets for experiments

questions.question: Diagrams can help explain electromagnetic radiation by showing variables, arrows, or relationships.
questions.explanation: Physics diagrams connect observations to causes and effects.

questions.question: Which question is most useful when analyzing Electromagnetic Radiation?
questions.explanation: Cause-and-effect reasoning is central to Physics.
options: What is changing, and what causes the change?
What answer sounds longest?
Can I skip the vocabulary?
Can I ignore safety rules?

questions.question: The overall force after forces are combined is called the ____ force.
questions.explanation: Net force means the overall or combined force on an object.

questions.question: In 1–2 sentences, explain one everyday example of electromagnetic radiation.
questions.correctAnswer: Answers should name an example and connect it to the lesson concept.
questions.explanation: A good answer names an everyday situation and explains it using the lesson vocabulary.

questions.explanation: Drawing and labeling helps reveal the relationships.
options: Draw and label the situation before explaining it
Guess without reading the diagram
Memorize only the first sentence
Avoid checking explanations

questions.question: A complete scientific explanation should include evidence or a reason, not just a one-word answer.
questions.explanation: Science explanations should justify the answer.

questions.question: Which safety rule is always correct for student circuit work?
questions.explanation: Student circuit activities should use low-voltage batteries and safe materials only.
options: Use only safe low-voltage batteries when doing circuit activities
Test household outlets with bare wire
Use wet hands near electrical devices
Remove insulation from live wires

questions.question: A quantity with size and direction can be represented by an arrow called a ____.
questions.explanation: A vector has magnitude and direction and is often shown by an arrow.

questions.question: What is one misconception about electromagnetic radiation that you should avoid?
questions.correctAnswer: EM waves do not need air. Sound needs a medium, but light and other EM radiation can travel through a vacuum.
questions.explanation: The misconception alert in the lesson identifies a common incorrect idea.

questions.question: If a diagram for Electromagnetic Radiation has arrows, what should you check first?
questions.explanation: Arrows have meaning only when you know what they represent.
options: What each arrow represents and which object or wave it acts on
Only the arrow color
Whether the page has many words
Whether the answer is the longest option
